results.fact: Lake of the Woods camp elevation vs Pistol Pass
results.correct_value: Lake of the Woods sits at about 6,620 ft (~6,600 ft), roughly 500 ft below 7,100 ft Pistol Pass
results.evidence: USGS 3DEP elevation at the lake surface returns 6,623 ft, and the independent SRTM 30 m model returns 2,020 m (6,627 ft); both return ~7,070-7,100 ft at Pistol Pass. A trip report describes the camp as a mile down from the pass, and another reports about 1,600 ft of gain from the lake to the 8,371 ft summit (implying ~6,750 ft). The stored 7,300 ft pin and the 7,000-7,300 ft prose all sit above the pass the camp is reached by descending from.

results.fact: Line from camp to the east ridge
results.correct_value: The east ridge is climbed directly from the Lake of the Woods camp; crossing the pass south of Lake Mountain into the Monument-Lake basin belongs to the Monument Peak / west-slope approach
results.evidence: Two trip reports go from the lake straight up through the larches onto Lake Mountain's east ridge (1.9 h and ~90 min from camp), one noting the peak is 'right there' above the lake. The only report that crossed the pass south of Lake Mountain and dropped the far side did so to climb Monument and Lake's WEST slope, and the Monument-Lake basin description is the Monument approach. The east-ridge fields that routed over the pass were fixed in waypoint directions, approach, the base-finding note and the descent.

results.fact: Gain from Lake of the Woods camp to the summit
results.evidence: approach, climbing_route[0] and itinerary day 2 say 1,300-1,400 ft from camp; pitch_detail says ~1,600 ft. With the lake at ~6,620 ft (USGS and SRTM) and the summit at 8,371 ft, the net rise is ~1,750 ft, and one trip report says about 1,600 ft. Day 2's gainFt (1,300) is part of the itinerary total that equals gain_ft 7,300, so it cannot be changed alone, and no second source states the figure; left open.
